label: Bonus Class 1
title: Does English Have a Future Tense?
bigIdea: English verbs have no future ending (that is why many linguists say English has no future tense); English talks about the future with tools (will, be going to, the present continuous, the present simple), and we choose the tool by meaning: a prediction, a plan, an arrangement or a timetable.
bigIdeaAr: الفعل الإنجليزي ليس له نهاية خاصة بالمستقبل (ولهذا يقول كثير من اللغويين إن الإنجليزية ليس فيها زمن مستقبل)؛ والإنجليزية تتحدث عن المستقبل بأدوات (will و be going to والمضارع المستمر والمضارع البسيط)، ونختار الأداة حسب المعنى: توقّع أو خطة أو موعد مرتّب أو جدول مواعيد.
builtOn: Lesson 1: going to for plans (plan, visit, join, apply, move, start, scholarship, internship, schedule)
Lesson 2: will for predictions (predict, believe, probably, definitely, maybe, forecast, certain, unlikely)
Lesson 3: present continuous for fixed plans (meeting, traveling, attending, leaving, hosting, ticket, booking, guest list)
Lesson 4: past continuous (was/were + -ing) - used here to compare verb forms

objectives.en: I can explain why many linguists say English has no future tense, and give one argument for the other side.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أشرح لماذا يقول كثير من اللغويين إن الإنجليزية ليس فيها زمن مستقبل، وأن أذكر حجة للرأي الآخر.

objectives.en: I can choose will, be going to or the present continuous by meaning (prediction, decision now, promise, plan, evidence, arrangement).
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أختار will أو be going to أو المضارع المستمر حسب المعنى (توقّع، قرار لحظي، وعد، خطة، دليل، موعد مرتّب).

objectives.en: I can compare the English future with Arabic سـ / سوف / لن and avoid 'I will to go'.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أقارن المستقبل في الإنجليزية بـ سـ وسوف ولن في العربية، وأتجنب قول I will to go.

objectives.en: I can hear and say 'll, won't and gonna in natural speech.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أسمع وأنطق 'll و won't و gonna في الكلام الطبيعي.

keyTerms.meaning: In the strict linguistic sense: a change in the form of the verb itself to show time: walk / walked. (Many school grammars use 'tense' more loosely.)
An ending or change inside a word that adds grammar: -s, -ed, -ing.
A helper verb such as will, can, must, should. It never takes -s and is followed by the base verb.
What you think or believe will happen.
Something you have already decided to do.
A plan with a time, a place and usually other people: it is in the calendar.
When a normal word slowly becomes a grammar word: 'going (walking) to' became the future marker 'going to'.

facts.en: English verbs change their own form for only two tenses: present (walk, walks) and past (walked). There is no future ending: no English verb looks like 'walk-future'.
facts.ar: الفعل الإنجليزي يغيّر شكله لزمنين فقط: المضارع (walk, walks) والماضي (walked). لا توجد نهاية للمستقبل: لا يوجد فعل إنجليزي بصيغة خاصة بالمستقبل.

facts.en: Many languages do have one. Spanish 'hablaré' and French 'parlerai' both mean 'I will speak', and the ending does the job. Fun fact: these endings come from the Latin verb habere, 'to have': French parler + ai ('I have'), roughly 'I have to speak'.
facts.ar: لغات كثيرة لها هذه النهاية. hablaré في الإسبانية و parlerai في الفرنسية تعنيان 'سأتكلم'، والنهاية تؤدي المهمة. معلومة طريفة: هذه النهايات أصلها الفعل اللاتيني habere بمعنى 'يملك': في الفرنسية parler + ai (أي 'عندي')، فالمعنى تقريباً 'عليّ أن أتكلم'.

facts.en: So English uses tools instead: the modal will, the phrase be going to, the present continuous (I'm meeting Sara at 5) and the present simple for timetables (The bus leaves at 7). That is why many linguists say 'English has no future tense, but many ways to talk about the future'. Many school grammars and some linguists call will + verb 'the future tense'. Both sides have a point: it depends on whether 'tense' means a verb ending or a meaning.
facts.ar: لذلك تستخدم الإنجليزية أدوات بدلاً منها: الفعل الشكلي will، والعبارة be going to، والمضارع المستمر (I'm meeting Sara at 5)، والمضارع البسيط للجداول (The bus leaves at 7). ولهذا يقول كثير من اللغويين: 'لا يوجد زمن مستقبل في الإنجليزية، بل طرق كثيرة للحديث عن المستقبل'. وكثير من كتب القواعد المدرسية وبعض اللغويين يسمّون will + الفعل 'زمن المستقبل'. لكل رأي وجهة: الأمر يتوقف على معنى كلمة 'زمن': هل هو نهاية في الفعل أم معنى؟

facts.en: Future words are born from normal words. In Old English 'willan' meant 'to want' (we still say 'free will' and 'willing'). 'Going to' first meant real movement: 'I am going to London to see the king'. Slowly, over a few hundred years, it became a grammar word, and in fast speech it became 'gonna'. Linguists call this grammaticalization.
facts.ar: كلمات المستقبل تولد من كلمات عادية. في الإنجليزية القديمة كان willan يعني 'يريد' (ما زلنا نقول free will أي الإرادة الحرة). و going to كانت تعني الذهاب الحقيقي: 'أنا ذاهب إلى لندن لأرى الملك'، ثم أصبحت كلمة نحوية، وفي الكلام السريع صارت gonna. يسمّي اللغويون هذا 'التحوّل النحوي'.

facts.en: Arabic dialects seem to have done the same thing. In classical grammar, the Kufan grammarians said the prefix سـ is a short form of سوف, while the Basran grammarians treated them as two separate words. In Levantine Arabic, رح (رح روح) is usually traced to رايح, 'going', and many linguists trace the Egyptian future prefix هـ / حـ (هروح، حروح) to the same word: very like the English 'going to' story! Many Gulf speakers use بـ (بروح، بسير), and some also use راح (راح أروح). Careful: in Egyptian and Levantine Arabic, بـ (بروح) usually means 'I go / I'm going' (present), not the future.
facts.ar: ويبدو أن اللهجات العربية فعلت الشيء نفسه. في النحو القديم رأى الكوفيون أن السين مقتطعة من سوف، ورأى البصريون أنهما حرفان مستقلان. وفي اللهجة الشامية يُرجَع 'رح' (رح روح) عادةً إلى 'رايح' أي ذاهب، ويرجع كثير من اللغويين بادئة المستقبل المصرية هـ / حـ (هروح، حروح) إلى الكلمة نفسها: إنها تشبه كثيراً قصة going to الإنجليزية! وكثير من المتكلمين في الخليج يستخدمون الباء (بروح، بسير)، وبعضهم يستخدم 'راح' (راح أروح). انتبه: في المصرية والشامية تعني 'بروح' غالباً 'أذهب' (المضارع) لا المستقبل.

arabicBridge.english: will go / am going to go / am going (tomorrow)
arabicBridge.point: Arabic mostly uses one form (سـ or سوف + the present verb) for every future meaning. English chooses between several forms depending on meaning, so translate the meaning, not the words.
arabicBridge.pointAr: العربية تستخدم غالباً صيغة واحدة (سـ أو سوف + المضارع) لكل معاني المستقبل، أما الإنجليزية فتختار بين عدة صيغ حسب المعنى؛ لذلك نترجم المعنى لا الكلمات.

arabicBridge.english: will + base verb (no 'to'): I will go
arabicBridge.arabic: سوف + فعل مضارع مباشرة: سوف أذهب
arabicBridge.point: Same pattern: سوف is followed directly by the verb, and so is will. Do not add 'to' after will. But 'going to' needs 'to': I'm going to go.
arabicBridge.pointAr: النمط نفسه: سوف يأتي بعدها الفعل مباشرة، وكذلك will. لا نضيف to بعد will. أما going to فتحتاج to.

arabicBridge.point: Both languages have a special negative for the future: لن in Arabic, won't in English. 'I won't be late' = لن أتأخر.
arabicBridge.pointAr: في اللغتين نفي خاص بالمستقبل: لن في العربية و won't في الإنجليزية.

arabicBridge.english: I'm meeting the coach tomorrow. / The bus leaves at 7.
arabicBridge.arabic: أقابل المدرب غداً. / يغادر الباص الساعة السابعة.
arabicBridge.point: Arabic can also use a plain present verb with a time word for the near future. English does this too, but with the present continuous for personal arrangements and the present simple mainly for timetables and schedules.
arabicBridge.pointAr: العربية أيضاً تستخدم المضارع العادي مع كلمة زمن للمستقبل القريب. والإنجليزية كذلك، لكن بالمضارع المستمر للمواعيد الشخصية، وبالمضارع البسيط للجداول والمواعيد الرسمية غالباً.

arabicBridge.point: Spoken English shortens the future (I'll, gonna), a bit like spoken Arabic dialects, which use short future markers such as رح and هـ / حـ (probably from رايح). Gonna is fine in chat and speech, not in formal writing.
arabicBridge.pointAr: الإنجليزية المحكية تختصر المستقبل (I'll, gonna) كما تستخدم اللهجات العربية علامات مستقبل قصيرة مثل رح و هـ / حـ (وأصلها على الأرجح رايح). gonna مقبولة في الكلام والدردشة لا في الكتابة الرسمية.

commonErrors.wrong: I will to go to the science fair.
commonErrors.right: I will go to the science fair.
commonErrors.why: Mixing will with 'going to'. will is a modal: it is followed directly by the base verb, like سوف أذهب.

commonErrors.wrong: I going to visit my cousins.
commonErrors.right: I'm going to visit my cousins.
commonErrors.why: Arabic has no 'be' verb in the present (أنا ذاهب), so am/is/are disappears. going to always needs am/is/are.

commonErrors.wrong: Tomorrow I go to my uncle.
commonErrors.right: Tomorrow I'm going to my uncle's. / I'm visiting my uncle tomorrow.
commonErrors.why: Arabic أذهب غداً uses the plain present. In English the present simple is mainly for timetables and schedules; for personal plans use the present continuous or going to.

commonErrors.wrong: He will goes / He wills go.
commonErrors.why: Modals never take -s and the verb after them stays in the base form.

commonErrors.wrong: Look at those black clouds! It will rain.
commonErrors.right: Look at those black clouds! It's going to rain.
commonErrors.why: Not impossible, but when we can see the evidence now, English strongly prefers going to. will is more typical for opinions and beliefs (I think it will rain next week).

commonErrors.wrong: (The phone rings.) I'm going to answer it!
commonErrors.right: I'll get it! / I'll answer it!
commonErrors.why: A decision made at the moment of speaking uses will ('ll). going to is for decisions made before.

commonErrors.right: I don't think it will rain.
commonErrors.why: Not wrong grammatically, but English usually puts the negative on think. Arabic أعتقد أنها لن تمطر pushes learners to the first form.

commonErrors.right: I'm going to the mall. / I'm gonna go to the mall.
commonErrors.why: gonna only replaces 'going to' + verb. When 'to' is a preposition before a place, we never say gonna.

teacher: A 'Future Forecast' image (Lumi as a TV weather-style forecaster) for the warm-up and the game
Verb-form table slide (walk / walks / walked / walking / will walk) and the language comparison slide (Spanish, French, Arabic)
Crew calendar slide: Omar, Sara, Noor, Ziad and Hamad's week with fixed times
The Future Toolbox slide: four tools with icons (forecast screen = will, notebook = going to, calendar = present continuous, train timetable = present simple)
student: Three paper cards: W (will), G (going to), C (present continuous)
Their real calendar or phone schedule for next week (optional)

stages.name: Warm-up: Lumi's Future Forecast
stages.purpose: Get students talking about the future at once and plant the question: which word in these sentences carries the future?
teacherSays: Welcome to Lumi's Future Forecast! Here are my (just for fun) forecasts... Omar, I think you will become a famous engineer. Sara, you told me you're going to apply for a scholarship. Noor, you're meeting a new friend on Friday, right? It's in your calendar!
Now you are the forecaster. Make one fun prediction about the next person in our group list. Start with: 'My forecast: I think you will...'
Quick question: in all these sentences, which word tells us it is the future? Is it the verb itself? Keep that question in your head.
teacherSaysAr: مرحباً بكم في نشرة لومي للمستقبل! هذه توقعاتي (للمرح فقط)...
الآن أنت مقدّم النشرة: قل توقعاً واحداً طريفاً عن الزميل التالي في القائمة.
سؤال: ما الكلمة التي تخبرنا أن الجملة عن المستقبل؟ هل هو الفعل نفسه؟
studentsDo: Listen to the teacher's predictions and react (Really? No way!).
Each student makes one prediction for a classmate: 'My forecast: I think you will...'.
Write in the chat the one word that shows the future in their sentence.
tips: Keep predictions positive and funny; teens enjoy exaggeration (You will have one million followers).
Collect the words from the chat (will, going to, 'm meeting) and leave them on screen for the next stage.

stages.name: Linguistics Corner: The Tense Detective
stages.method: Guided discovery + cross-language comparison + mini vote (debate seed)
stages.purpose: Discover that English verbs only inflect for present and past, compare with Spanish, French and Arabic, and meet the 'no future tense' debate.
teacherSays: Look at the verb walk. Walk, walks, walked, walking. The verb itself changes for present and for past. Where is the future form?
Exactly: there is no 'walk-future'. To talk about the future we add a helper: will walk, am going to walk, am walking tomorrow.
Now look at Spanish: hablo = I speak, hablaré = I will speak. The ending -é carries the future. In Arabic: أمشي, سأمشي. Arabic adds the prefix سـ to the verb.

So here is the big debate. Some linguists say: English has no future tense, only two tenses, present and past. Others say: will + verb is the future tense. What do you think? Vote now: thumbs up for 'no future tense', thumbs down for 'yes, it has one'.
One more secret: will once meant 'want' in Old English, and 'going to' once meant real walking. Words change their jobs over time. Linguists call it grammaticalization.
teacherSaysAr: الفعل الإنجليزي يتغير شكله للمضارع وللماضي فقط. أين صيغة المستقبل؟ لا توجد!
في الإسبانية النهاية تحمل المستقبل، وفي العربية نضيف السين إلى الفعل.
صوّتوا: هل في الإنجليزية زمن مستقبل أم لا؟ لكل رأي حجته.
studentsDo: Complete the verb-form table on the slide (walk, walks, walked, walking, was walking, will walk).
Circle the part that shows time in each language example.
Vote and give one reason in one sentence: 'I think English has / doesn't have a future tense because...'.

exercise.instructions: What shows the time: a change in the verb itself (ending/prefix) or a separate helper word? Sort each example.
exercise.instructionsAr: ما الذي يدل على الزمن: تغيير في الفعل نفسه (نهاية أو سابقة) أم كلمة مساعدة منفصلة؟ صنّف كل مثال.

items.prompt: walked
items.answer: change in the verb (-ed = past)

items.prompt: walks
items.answer: change in the verb (-s = present)

items.prompt: will walk
items.answer: separate helper word (will)

items.prompt: is going to walk
items.answer: separate helper words (is going to)

items.prompt: is walking tomorrow
items.answer: separate helper word (is) + time word (tomorrow); the -ing alone does not mean future

items.prompt: hablaré (Spanish)
items.answer: change in the verb (ending -é = future)

items.prompt: سأمشي
items.answer: change in the verb (prefix سـ = future)

items.prompt: سوف أمشي
items.answer: separate helper word (سوف)

tips: Present the debate honestly: both views are respectable. The useful conclusion is that English future = tools chosen by meaning.
Note the nice twist: Arabic has both systems - a prefix (سـ) and a separate word (سوف).

stages.name: Arabic Bridge: One Arabic Future, Many English Futures
stages.nameAr: جسر العربية: مستقبل عربي واحد ومستقبلات إنجليزية كثيرة
stages.purpose: Show that سأفعل can become will, going to or the present continuous in English, so students translate meaning, not words.
teacherSays: In Arabic, سأساعدك, سأسافر, سأقابل all use the same سـ. English asks a question first: is it a prediction, a promise, a plan or an arrangement?
Remember: سوف + verb, will + verb. No 'to' in the middle. But with going to, 'to' must stay.
And the negative: لن أتأخر = I won't be late. Both languages have a special word for 'not in the future'.
Your Arabic dialect is a secret weapon: Levantine رح probably comes from رايح, 'going'. English going to also came from 'going'. A very similar idea in two languages!
teacherSaysAr: العربية تستخدم السين لكل المعاني، أما الإنجليزية فتسأل أولاً: هل هو توقع أم وعد أم خطة أم موعد؟
سوف + فعل، will + فعل، بلا to. أما going to فلا بد من to.
لن أتأخر = I won't be late.
studentsDo: Read each Arabic sentence and its situation, then decide the meaning (prediction, promise, decision now, plan, evidence, arrangement, timetable).
Translate into English using the best tool; hold up the W, G or C card first.
Compare answers in pairs and explain one choice.

exercise.instructions: Read the Arabic sentence and the situation. Write the best English sentence.
exercise.instructionsAr: اقرأ الجملة العربية والموقف، ثم اكتب أفضل جملة بالإنجليزية.

items.prompt: سأساعدك! (Your friend drops all her books right now.)
items.answer: I'll help you! (will: decision at the moment / offer)

items.prompt: سأتقدم للمنحة السنة القادمة. (You decided last month.)
items.answer: I'm going to apply for the scholarship next year. (going to: intention)

items.prompt: سأقابل المدرب يوم الأحد الساعة الرابعة. (It is in your calendar.)
items.answer: I'm meeting the coach on Sunday at 4. (present continuous: arrangement; also accept I'm going to meet...)

items.prompt: ستمطر! انظر إلى الغيوم السوداء.
items.answer: It's going to rain! Look at the black clouds. (going to: evidence now)

items.prompt: أعتقد أن فريقنا سيفوز.
items.answer: I think our team will win. (will: opinion / prediction)

items.prompt: لن أتأخر، أعدك.
items.answer: I won't be late, I promise. (will: promise)

items.prompt: تغادر الطائرة الساعة السابعة صباحاً. (Airport timetable.)
items.answer: The plane leaves at 7 a.m. (present simple: timetable)

items.prompt: سننتقل إلى مدينة جديدة. (Your parents already decided.)
items.answer: We're going to move to a new city. (going to: plan; also accept We're moving...)

tips: Items 3 and 8 have two good answers (present continuous or going to): accept both and discuss the small difference.
Students often want one 'correct' answer; teach them that English often allows two forms with a slightly different message.

stages.name: The Future Toolbox: Meaning Map with the Crew
stages.nameAr: صندوق أدوات المستقبل: خريطة المعاني مع الفريق
stages.method: Guided discovery from mini-dialogues + rule-writing by students
stages.purpose: Students write the rules for will, going to and the present continuous themselves from crew examples, then apply them.
teacherSays: Here are six mini-scenes from the crew. Read them and find the tool each person uses.

Scene 1: Omar's phone rings. 'I'll get it!' Scene 2: Sara: 'I'm going to apply for an internship this summer.' Scene 3: Noor: 'I'm meeting the coach at 4 tomorrow. It's in my calendar.' Scene 4: Ziad looks at the sky: 'It's going to rain.' Scene 5: Hamad: 'Our team will definitely win the final!' Scene 6: Lumi: 'The science fair starts at 9.'
Now you are the grammar writers. Complete the rules: We use will for... We use going to for... We use the present continuous for... We use the present simple for...
Great rules! Now test them.
teacherSaysAr: اقرؤوا المشاهد الستة واكتشفوا الأداة التي يستخدمها كل شخص.
الآن أنتم من يكتب القاعدة: نستخدم will لـ... ونستخدم going to لـ...
studentsDo: Match each scene to a tool and a meaning.
In pairs, write the four rules in their own words on the shared slide.
Compare with the teacher's Future Toolbox slide and correct their rules.
Do the choose-the-tool exercise and justify each answer with a meaning word.

exercise.instructions: Choose the best form and say why (prediction, decision now, promise, plan, evidence, arrangement, timetable).

items.prompt: A: I'm thirsty. B: Wait, I ___ (get) you some water.
items.answer: 'll get (decision now / offer)

items.prompt: Sara has bought her ticket. She ___ (travel) to Cairo on Thursday.
items.answer: is traveling (arrangement; also accept is going to travel)

items.prompt: I believe robots ___ (do) most jobs in 2050.
items.answer: will do (prediction / belief)

items.prompt: Ziad has decided: he ___ (join) the robotics team next term.
items.answer: is going to join (intention / plan; also accept is joining)

items.prompt: Look! Hamad is running too fast with that tray. He ___ (drop) it!
items.answer: is going to drop (evidence now)

items.prompt: The train to Dubai ___ (leave) at 6:45 tomorrow morning.
items.answer: leaves (timetable)

items.prompt: Don't worry, Mum. I ___ (not / forget) your birthday this year.
items.answer: won't forget (promise)

items.prompt: We ___ (host) a party on Saturday. The guest list is ready.
items.answer: are hosting (arrangement; also accept are going to host)

items.prompt: The forecast says it ___ (be) sunny all weekend.
items.answer: will be (prediction from a source; also accept is going to be)

items.prompt: Noor ___ (meet) her cousins at the airport at 8. Her dad booked it.
items.answer: is meeting (arrangement; also accept is going to meet)

tips: Several items have two good answers (shown in the key). The going to / present continuous line is fuzzy for native speakers too: if a plan has a time, a place and other people, the present continuous sounds most natural.
Ask 'Why?' after every answer; the reason is the real learning.
Keep the four-icon toolbox slide visible for the rest of the class.

stages.name: Sound of the Future: 'll, won't, gonna + Error Clinic
stages.nameAr: صوت المستقبل: 'll و won't و gonna + عيادة الأخطاء
stages.method: Listening discrimination + pronunciation drill + error correction
stages.purpose: Hear and say the weak forms of the future, then fix the typical errors of Arabic speakers.
teacherSays: In real English, will is almost always short: I'll, you'll, she'll, we'll. Listen: I'll call you. I'll call you. Can you hear the 'll?
Be careful: won't and want sound close. won't rhymes with 'don't'. 'I won't go' = لن أذهب. 'I want to go' = أريد أن أذهب. Big difference!
Gonna is how people say 'going to' + verb in fast speech: I'm gonna study. But never 'I'm gonna the mall'.
Now the Error Clinic: you are the doctors. Each sentence is sick. Find the problem and cure it.
teacherSaysAr: will تُختصر غالباً في الكلام: I'll, she'll.
انتبهوا: won't تعني 'لن'، و want تعني 'يريد'.
gonna تحل محل going to + فعل فقط.
studentsDo: Listen to 6 sentences and write if they hear 'll or nothing (I'll call / I call).
Listen and decide: won't or want?
Say the sentences with contractions in a chain around the group.
Correct the 8 sick sentences and explain the cure.

exercise.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Find it and correct it.
exercise.instructionsAr: في كل جملة خطأ واحد. اكتشفه وصححه.

items.prompt: I will to visit my grandmother on Friday.
items.answer: I will visit my grandmother on Friday.

items.prompt: She going to start a new hobby.
items.answer: She's going to start a new hobby.

items.prompt: Tomorrow I go to the dentist at 10. (personal appointment)
items.answer: Tomorrow I'm going to the dentist at 10. / Tomorrow I'm going to go to the dentist at 10.

items.prompt: He will plays in the final.
items.answer: He will play in the final.

items.prompt: Look at that car! It will crash!
items.answer: Look at that car! It's going to crash!

items.prompt: I'm gonna the science fair.
items.answer: I'm going to the science fair. / I'm gonna go to the science fair.

items.prompt: Are you come to my party on Saturday?
items.answer: Are you coming to my party on Saturday?

items.prompt: I think it won't be difficult.
items.answer: I don't think it will be difficult. (more natural)

tips: Item 8 is about naturalness, not a hard error: tell students both are understood. Item 5 is a strong preference (evidence now = going to); 'It'll crash!' is possible in a shout, so do not argue about it.
If a student pronounces won't like want, try lip-rounding: won't has an 'o' shape, like 'own' with a w.

stages.name: Forecast Studio and the Crew Calendar
stages.method: Gamified team challenge (certainty scale) + information-gap role-play
stages.purpose: Use will with certainty adverbs for predictions and the present continuous for arrangements in free, personal speech.
teacherSays: Round 1: Forecast Studio. Two teams. Make predictions about the world in 2040: phones, schools, cars, football, food. Use the certainty scale: will definitely, will probably, probably won't, definitely won't, it's unlikely that...
Careful with word order: 'will probably' but 'probably won't'. The adverb goes after will but before won't.
The other team answers: I agree / I don't think so. Best prediction wins a point.

Round 2: Crew Calendar. You are Noor, Ziad, Sara or Hamad. Your calendar is on your slide. Ask each other: What are you doing on Friday evening? Are you free on Sunday? Find a time when all of you can play a board game.
teacherSaysAr: الجولة الأولى: توقّعوا شكل العالم سنة 2040 باستخدام درجات اليقين.
انتبهوا للترتيب: will probably لكن probably won't.
الجولة الثانية: أنتم شخصيات الفريق، اسألوا عن مواعيد بعضكم واتفقوا على وقت مشترك.
studentsDo: Team task: write 5 predictions for 2040 on the shared slide using different certainty levels.
Read predictions aloud; the other team reacts and votes.
Put the adverb in the right place in the sentence-builder exercise.
Role-play: ask and answer about the week with the present continuous until they find a free slot, then agree with will: 'OK, I'll bring the game!'

exercise.instructions: Put the words in the right order to make a prediction.
exercise.instructionsAr: رتّب الكلمات لتكوّن جملة توقّع صحيحة.

items.prompt: will / cars / fly / probably / in 2040
items.answer: Cars will probably fly in 2040.

items.prompt: won't / definitely / paper books / disappear
items.answer: Paper books definitely won't disappear.

items.prompt: unlikely / it's / that / will / rain / it / tomorrow
items.answer: It's unlikely that it will rain tomorrow.

items.prompt: certain / I'm / win / we / will
items.answer: I'm certain we will win.

items.prompt: probably / schools / won't / have / homework
items.answer: Schools probably won't have homework.

items.prompt: believe / I / will / a cure / scientists / find
items.answer: I believe scientists will find a cure.

tips: Give each student a slightly different calendar so they really need to ask (information gap).
Reward reasons: 'Cars will probably fly because...' earns a bonus point.
Correct only the target forms during the game; note other errors for the end.

stages.name: Exit Ticket, Did You Know? and Goodbye
stages.method: Formative check + debate recap + curiosity close
stages.purpose: Check that every student can choose the right future form and explain the big idea in one sentence.
teacherSays: Exit ticket! Five sentences. Write only the missing words. You have three minutes.
Last word on our debate: Does English have a future tense? Say your answer in one sentence and one reason.

Did you know? Some languages, such as Chinese (Mandarin), have no tense endings at all, not even for the past. They use time words like 'yesterday' and 'tomorrow' and small helper words. And people still talk about the future perfectly well!
Your mission: tonight, tell someone at home about one plan, one arrangement and one prediction in English.
teacherSaysAr: هل تعلم؟ بعض اللغات مثل الصينية ليس فيها نهايات للأزمنة أصلاً، حتى للماضي، وتستخدم كلمات مثل 'أمس' و'غداً'.
مهمتك: أخبر أحداً في البيت عن خطة وموعد وتوقّع بالإنجليزية.
studentsDo: Complete the 5 exit-ticket items.
Say their final debate answer with a reason.
Say goodbye with a promise: 'I'll do my homework!'
tips: Students under 4/5 need a toolbox reminder in the warm-ups of Lessons 5-8 (Lesson 8 reviews going to).
Accept any well-argued answer to the debate; the reason matters more than the side.

exitTicket.instructions: Complete each sentence with the best future form.
exitTicket.instructionsAr: أكمل كل جملة بأفضل صيغة للمستقبل.

items.prompt: (The doorbell rings.) Don't move, I ___ (open) it.
items.answer: 'll open

items.prompt: I ___ (meet) Omar at the mall at 5. We booked a table.
items.answer: 'm meeting (also accept 'm going to meet)

items.prompt: She has decided. She ___ (join) the football team.
items.answer: is going to join (also accept 's joining)

items.prompt: I think it ___ (be) a great year.
items.answer: will be (also accept 's going to be)

items.prompt: Correct the mistake: I will to call you tonight.
items.answer: I will call you tonight.

homework.en: Future Diary: write a short diary page about next week (8-10 sentences) with at least two arrangements (present continuous), two plans (going to), two predictions (will + probably/definitely) and one promise (won't).
homework.ar: مذكرات المستقبل: اكتب صفحة قصيرة عن الأسبوع القادم (8-10 جمل) فيها موعدان مرتبان (المضارع المستمر)، وخطتان (going to)، وتوقعان (will + probably/definitely)، ووعد واحد (won't).
tasks: Write the Future Diary and underline each future tool in a different color.
Find one future sentence in a song, a video or a game in English and decide which tool it uses.
Ask a family member how to say 'I will go' in their dialect (سأذهب، هروح، بروح، رح روح...) and write it down.

support: Work with two tools first (will for predictions/decisions now, going to for plans), then add the present continuous.
Give a sentence frame for every task: 'I'm going to ___ because I decided...'.
Let students hold up the W/G/C card before writing the full sentence.
challenge: Add the present simple for timetables and explain why 'The match starts at 8' is fine but 'I go to the dentist tomorrow' sounds odd.
Prepare a 1-minute argument for or against 'English has a future tense' with two reasons.
Compare 'I'll see you tomorrow' and 'I'm seeing you tomorrow': what is the difference in feeling?

successCriteria: Explains in English or Arabic that English verbs only change form for present and past, and names at least three future tools.
Chooses the correct form in at least 8 of 10 choose-and-justify items and gives a meaning reason.
Produces at least two correct predictions with will + certainty adverb in the right position.
Uses the present continuous for at least two arrangements in the calendar role-play.
watchFor: missing be in going to (I going to)
present simple for personal plans (Tomorrow I go to...)

teacherNotes: The 'no future tense' claim is a real scholarly position (based on inflection), but some grammars call will + verb a future tense. Present it as an open debate; the practical message is to choose tools by meaning.
Lesson 4 was about the past continuous; use it briefly in the verb-form table to show that English changes the verb form only for present and past, and builds everything else with helpers.
Do not punish going to vs present continuous mix-ups for arrangements: both are often acceptable. Focus on the clear errors (will to, missing be, present simple for plans).
Bonus Class 2 continues with the modal must and with have to (which behaves like a normal verb): students already know that modals take no -s and no 'to'.
